title: Spit-up vs vomiting — what's normal?
summary: Most spit-up is normal. Vomiting is a different pattern and needs attention.
whatsNormal:
Spit-up (reflux) is common in healthy newborns. It is usually small amounts that dribble out after feeds, and your baby is comfortable between episodes.

• Happens during or shortly after feeding
• Baby seems content afterward
• Steady weight gain at checkups
• No forceful projection across the room

Almost all babies spit up sometimes. It often improves around 4–6 months.
watchFor: Spit-up becoming more frequent or larger over a few days
Arching, crying, or discomfort during or after feeds
Poor weight gain or falling off the growth curve
Refusing feeds or extreme fussiness around feeding time
callDoctorIf: Forceful vomiting (projectile) or vomit that shoots out
Fever in a baby under 3 months
Baby seems in pain or cannot keep any milk down
